title: Levelwise K-injective towers compute additive functors applied levelwise
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive functor [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Write $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ and similarly for $\mathcal B$, with levelwise exactness, and let $G^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ apply $G$ levelwise. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $RG^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ be the total right derived functor obtained by resolving a strict tower complex by a K-injective tower complex and applying $G^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ termwise. Here a tower complex $Q$ is K-injective when every chain map from an acyclic tower complex to $Q$ is null-homotopic; for ordinary module complexes use [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. If $X$ is a strict tower complex whose every evaluation $X_n$ is K-injective, then for every K-injective tower resolution $q:X\to Q$, every evaluation $Q_n$ is K-injective and
$$G^{\operatorname{Tow}}(q):G^{\operatorname{Tow}}X\longrightarrow G^{\operatorname{Tow}}Q$$
is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism. Consequently the canonical comparison $G^{\operatorname{Tow}}X\to RG^{\operatorname{Tow}}X$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal B))$, natural on the category of such $X$ and compatible with their strict transitions. In particular, if $X$ has the same K-injective complex $J$ at every level and a chain endomorphism $s:J\to J$ as each transition, its derived image is represented by the actual tower with terms $GJ$ and transitions $G(s)$.
